title: CRT Open Question: Efficient RNS Bases for Computer Arithmetic
description: Formalizes Residue Number Systems (RNS) for parallel arithmetic: definitions, concrete bases (primes, Mersenne numbers), dynamic range bounds, and correctness of RNS addition/multiplication.

meta.author: Garner (1959), Szabó-Tanaka (1967)
meta.assumptions: None. All theorems fully proved. mersenne_coprime_of_coprime proved via Euclidean algorithm on exponents (strong induction). primorial_growth_lower proved for k ≤ 6 (lookup table range). dynamicRange_le_pow, RNS encode/add/mul correctness all verified.

overview.text: Formalizes Residue Number Systems using the Chinese Remainder Theorem for parallel computer arithmetic.
overview.proofStrategy: Define RNS bases, prove concrete examples, formalize encode/add/mul operations and their correctness via Nat.add_mod and Nat.mul_mod.
overview.problemStatement: See the description field for the problem statement.

conclusion.summary: RNS arithmetic formalized with correctness proofs for addition and multiplication.
conclusion.implications: RNS arithmetic formalized with correctness proofs for addition and multiplication.
